note: The Duel's announcer: every moment's lines, 1-3 each, original English with the odd Japanese hype word (hajime, ikuzo, sugoi, kanpeki, yatta, mada mada, sore made). No line quotes or names any other work, character, technique, show or game; the voice is the game's own announcer (see voiceDesign), never a person's or a known announcer's. src/audio/duelCaller.ts calls the moments (DUEL_CALLER: priority, chance, rest) and reads the recorded takes from src/audio/data/duelCaller.json by voice and moment; a moment a voice has no line for borrows the Rift announcer's fitting line (duelCaller.ts BORROWED) or stays quiet.
archetype: An anime tournament announcer: a big, bright, theatrical voice from the arena's booth, hype that rises with the fight, crisp on the short calls and roaring on the big ones, now and then a Japanese hype word. The voice is the Rift's announcer's, the game's own.
voiceDesign: The game's own announcer: the Rift's voice, designed for the game with Qwen3-TTS from a description (no person cloned) and spoken in it (public/assets/audio/survival/announcer-*.m4a). Its design take was no longer at hand, so the voice was cloned (ElevenLabs Instant Voice Cloning) from its own 77 shipped lines, as they ship (the clone that kept the room scored closest to the original), and the Duel's lines are spoken in that clone.
generation: The six lines the announcer already says word for word (Round one!, Round two!, Final round!, Fight!, Victory!, Flawless!) are its own shipped takes. Every other line: three takes in the clone (eleven_v3, stability 0.5, an audio tag from the line's `how`), each heard by Whisper (large-v3-turbo) and measured against the shipped lines (a speaker embedding's cosine to their centroid: the clone's kept takes 0.81 on average, the shipped lines 0.84 against each other, five other designed voices 0.67); the take that says the line, fits under maxSeconds where one does, and sounds closest is kept. Prepared as the ball caller's lines are (trimmed, the loudest 400 ms at -13 LUFS as the Rift's are, 48 kHz mono AAC) into public/assets/audio/duel/caller/rift/<id>.m4a, listed in src/audio/data/duelCaller.json by moment.
